newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks continue higher after record close.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks continue higher after record close.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks continued to move ahead in Thursday morning trade, with the Hang Seng index benefiting from follow-through buying after rallying to a record close on Wednesday.
The Hang Seng index was up 73.43 points at 12,324.00 after jumping 143.81 points to a record close of 12,250.57 on Wednesday. Turnover was HK$1.73 billion after the first 50 minutes of trade.
"I think the momentum is quite strong," said Patrick Chia, research director at China Everbright Research.

"In the near term the Hang Seng index can test higher levels. Yesterday's rally was strong," he said. "I guess there is buying interest from overseas which is expected to push the index to test the record high at 12,600 in the medium term."
One trader said she was seeing very little profit-taking.

"No one is going to sell the Hong Kong market...We still see money coming in," she said. "Even if Hongkong Bank falls HK$10 no one is going to sell it. If you sell Hongkong Bank where are you going to put your money?"
Property and banking stocks, which led the charge on Wednesday, continued higher.
Cheung Kong rose HK$0.25 to HK$62.25 and Sun Hung Kai Properties advanced HK$0.25 to HK$86.25. Henderson Land was up HK$0.25 to HK$70.00 and New World Development rose HK$0.40 to HK$41.70.
"For Hong Kong there are still positive factors that fuel the buying interest like the property market. Everybody is expecting a further pick up in the final quarter of this year," said one analyst.
In the banking sector, HSBC Holdings (Hongkong Bank) rose HK$1.00 to HK$148.50, Hang Seng Bank gained HK$0.25 at HK$87.25 and Bank of East Asia was up HK$0.05 at HK$29.30.
Utilities came under some selling pressure with Hongkong Telecom slipping HK$0.10 to HK$14.00 and Hongkong & China Gas down HK$0.05 at HK$13.10.
The H-share index advanced 12 points to 860.
